subject: general
question: When the selling price of a TV is ​₹ 18,700, the shopkeeper incurs a loss of 15%. What should be the selling price of that TV so as to gain 15%?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Loss of 15% means **SP₁** = 100% − 15% = 85%.

Gain of 15% means **SP₂** = 100% + 15% = 115%.

According to the question, 85% = ₹ 18,700.

Unitary method: 1% = 18,700 ÷ 85 = ₹ 220.

Therefore, 115% = 220 × 115 = ₹ 25,300.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹ 25,300.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** First Selling Price (SP₁) = ₹ 18,700, Loss% = 15%, Required Profit% = 15%.

**Formulas:** CP = SP × 100 ÷ (100 − Loss%) | SP = CP × (100 + Gain%) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1cb7b566197ec3b3fb1061e5017945f4dc973a75c648bd5554237f0d9d10b3da.png] 

⇒ **Cost Price (CP)** = 18,700 × 100 ÷ (100 − 15) = 18,700 × 100 ÷ 85 = ₹ 22,000.

⇒ **New Selling Price (SP₂)** = 22,000 × (100 + 15) ÷ 100 = 22,000 × 115 ÷ 100.

⇒ SP₂ = 220 × 115 = ₹ 25,300.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹ 25,300.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cost Price (CP)

The price at which an article is purchased. It is always considered as 100% in percentage calculations of profit or loss.

Selling Price (SP)

The price at which an article is sold. SP = CP + Profit OR SP = CP − Loss.
